rm-01-pecado.context: Paul has just shown that Jews and Gentiles are under sin. Now he announces how God's righteousness has been revealed in Christ, apart from works of the law.
rm-01-pecado.focusQuestion: What changes when you stop trying to justify yourself and trust in Christ?
rm-01-pecado.keywordGloss: God acts justly and declares righteous those who believe in Jesus.
facts: No one will be justified before God by works of the law.
God's righteousness has been revealed apart from the law.
All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
Those who believe are justified freely, by his grace.
God is just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.

rm-02-justificacao.context: Paul showed that God justifies those who believe, as Abraham believed. Now he describes what changes in the life of someone justified by faith.
rm-02-justificacao.focusQuestion: How does peace with God change the way you get through a hard day?
rm-02-justificacao.keywordGloss: Whoever is justified by faith is no longer at war with God, but at peace with him.
facts: Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ.
Through Christ we have access by faith to the grace in which we stand.
We boast in the hope of the glory of God.
Tribulation produces perseverance.
Perseverance produces experience, and experience, hope.

rm-03-vida-espirito.context: Paul showed the struggle with sin and freedom in Christ. Now he announces the new life of those who are in Christ and walk by the Spirit.
rm-03-vida-espirito.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you want to walk by the Spirit today?
rm-03-vida-espirito.keywordGloss: God's Spirit sets free from sin and death and directs the new life in Christ.
reflectionPrompts: A mind led by the Spirit
facts: There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
The law of the Spirit of life set Paul free from the law of sin and death.
God sent his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.
The law's requirement is fulfilled in those who live not by the flesh but by the Spirit.
Those who lean toward the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

rm-04-israel.context: Paul reflected on Israel, the Gentiles and God's plans in Romans 9-11. He closes the topic by showing mercy for all and bursting into praise.
rm-04-israel.focusQuestion: Facing plans of God you do not fully understand, how can you respond with trust?
rm-04-israel.keywordGloss: God shows mercy to all, even in the face of everyone's disobedience.
reflectionPrompts: All from him and to him
facts: Those who were once disobedient received mercy because of their disobedience.
God placed all under disobedience in order to show mercy to all.
God's wisdom and knowledge are deep.
God's judgments are unsearchable and his ways inscrutable.
From him, through him and to him are all things.

rm-05-culto.context: After announcing mercy for all, Paul calls the church to respond. Grace received becomes a body offered, a renewed mind and life together.
rm-05-culto.focusQuestion: What concrete part of your life can you present to God today?
rm-05-culto.keywordGloss: The whole life presented to God as a living sacrifice is the worship he asks for.
reflectionPrompts: The body as a living sacrifice
facts: Paul urges them to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God.
We must not conform to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of the mind.
So we can test and approve God's good, pleasing and perfect will.
No one should think of himself more highly than he ought, but with sober judgment.
Though many, we form one body in Christ and are members of one another.

rm-06-desafio.context: This challenge reviews all of Romans: everyone's sin, justification by faith, life in the Spirit, God's mercy and the worship of one's whole life.
rm-06-desafio.focusQuestion: In light of all God has done in Christ, what concrete response will you give today?
rm-06-desafio.keywordGloss: God justifies those who believe in Christ, sets free by the Spirit and turns life into worship.
facts: All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ.
There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
God placed all under disobedience in order to show mercy to all.
We should present our bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God.
Tribulation produces perseverance, and experience, hope.
